_about: Text rules: questions that go straight to the LLM agent without asking System-1. Checked in order on the lower-cased question, after the gate's built-in check that it opens like a yes/no question; the first rule that matches decides, and its reason is logged and returned in X-Gate-Reason. A rule matches when ANY of its 'any' patterns matches, or when ALL of its 'all' patterns match (Python regular expressions, re.search). Add your own: append a rule with a new reason. Every rule should err toward the LLM: a question wrongly caught costs one LLM call; one wrongly let through gets a yes/no shown that may be meaningless. The gate refuses to start if a rule is malformed. To use a file of your own, set GATE_TEXT_RULES to its path.

rules.example: Can you explain how interest is worked out?
rules.why: Polite requests for information or for an action, not yes/no questions; also a second layer for the action check.

Questions about this customer's records: the gate has none, the agent has the MCP tools. Keyed on the opening, not on the word 'my': general policy questions in the first person ('Can I access my account from any branch?') stay with System-1.

rules.example: Can my card be blocked right now?
rules.why: A request to act on an account or card now: a 'No.' to someone with a lost card is the worst answer this flow can give.

rules.example: Is it possible to block my card?
rules.why: A request to act, phrased as a question about what is possible: the agent's, not a bare yes/no. Shipped by default because the vLLM System-1 model's action veto carries no signal (SYSTEM1_MAX_P_ACTION=1.0). It errs toward the agent: it also catches information questions with an action verb. On the 391 test questions it matches 9, of which 8 are plain yes/no questions System-1 should answer ('Can I cancel a transaction') and 1 needs the agent but is already caught by the numbers rule; the requests it exists for do not occur in that set.
Numbers and amounts: System-1 is a classifier, not a calculator.

rules.example: Is APR yearly? And how is it worked out?
rules.why: Two questions in one: a single yes or no cannot answer both.
